steps: Install and reboot with PathGuard Next 0.1.19-dev enabled under SukiSU Ultra
Cold-start LocalSend 50 times after force-stop and record PID cleanup, runtime status, three rule mounts, launch telemetry and RSS for every cycle
Keep LocalSend alive for 50 home-to-foreground operations and record PID stability, runtime status, three rule mounts, Android launch telemetry and RSS
Enter the LocalSend mount namespace, copy its UID, GID and supplementary groups, then probe both deny paths and create a file through the logical redirect source
Prepare one LocalSend v2 upload session and upload a 131-byte TXT plus a 199241-byte JPG after the soak
Verify HTTP results, physical paths, payload hashes, source absence, Provider liveness, PathGuard route logs and the crash buffer
Force-stop LocalSend and verify process and namespace cleanup without stopping either system Provider
expected_result: The application mount and Provider adapters enforce the configured deny and redirect rules without invoking seccomp-forbidden openat2 in Android Providers, losing files, leaking mounts or crashing a Provider
before_actual: The 0.1.18-dev device run returned HTTP 500 for both TXT and JPG uploads with a LocalSend could-not-save response; the interactive diagnosis observed Provider SIGSYS on syscall 437 before the module reboot
after_actual: The 0.1.19-dev run passed all 50 functional cold start/status/mount checks; am reported COLD for 48 cycles and UNKNOWN for 2 cycles whose old PID cleanup, new runtime status and mounts still passed. A further 50 warm foreground operations retained one PID and passed every status/mount check, while Android reported UNKNOWN and TotalTime 0 for all already-running Activity launches, so no warm latency percentile is claimed. Post-soak TXT and JPG uploads returned HTTP 200, matched their Host SHA-256 values, existed only under Download/localsend-redirect, left both Providers alive and produced zero matching crash-buffer entries
reviewer_conclusion: The Provider openat2 removal is an intentional compatibility correction and the observed myron scenarios contain no remaining unexpected regression. The mount cancellation, rollback, owner-death and rollback-failure device submatrix is covered by the linked V-59 report. V-57 through V-62 remain partial because this is one arm64 device and does not cover the frozen multi-ROM, second-framework, Provider-restart, fanotify, policy/topology fault or complete operation matrices
